PullRequest.Title: agentHost: Resolve published MCP server lifecycle IDs
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #332072

## Problem

Agent Host start/stop handling reverse-resolved customization IDs only through the controller's runtime `_live` inventory. During a same-name collision, the runtime can first associate a server name with a published plugin child and then receive a distinct same-name workspace top-level customization.

Agent Customizations presents the workspace entry and sends its exact ID, but the live lookup no longer recognizes that ID. The provider logs `Cannot start unknown MCP server customization ...`, no server process starts, and the optimistic client reducer leaves the row at `Starting`.

## Change

Keep the runtime lookup as the first choice, then fall back to an exact-ID lookup across the session's currently published customizations.

The fallback accepts only an ID that is present in current session state. It does not add a broad same-name alias and does not change collision precedence. The SDK lifecycle API remains name-keyed, so it starts the effective server winner already selected for that name.

## Validation

- `npm run gulp compile-client`
- `npx mocha test/unit/node/index.js --delay --ui=tdd --timeout=20000 --exit --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/shared/mcpCustomizationController.test.ts` — 20 passing
- Targeted ESLint and `git diff --check`
- Regression coverage verifies published IDs resolve before the SDK has populated the live inventory and unknown IDs remain rejected.
- Deterministic live Code OSS A/B with a real Copilot Agent Host session and real local stdio MCP processes:
  - A host-only plugin published and started `dupe`; the real UI then stopped it through its plugin-child customization ID.
  - A workspace-root `.mcp.json` with another `dupe` was published afterward, producing two distinct current customization IDs with no synthetic `mcp-top-level:*` ID and no intervening SDK state event that could repair the mapping.
  - Unpatched main: the UI dispatched `SessionMcpServerStartRequested` with the exact workspace ID, Agent Host logged the matching unknown-customization warning, no process spawned, and the clicked row remained stuck at `Starting`.
  - Patched: the UI dispatched the same workspace ID, no unknown-customization warning was logged, a new real MCP process spawned, the workspace entry transitioned `stopped -> starting -> ready`, and the clicked row reached `Running`.
  - A separate `solo` server completed stop/start successfully as a control.
- The patched live arm was repeated through the repository's normal `scripts/code.bat` launch path with the same result.

Current source combines user and `.vscode/mcp.json` inputs before Agent Host receives them, so the live harness used a host-configured plugin child plus workspace-root `.mcp.json` to deterministically reproduce the same published child/top-level identity collision described by the issue.

Scenarios.Scenario: Copilot MCP start/stop for a customization ID that is published in current session state but not yet represented by the SDK live inventory
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A client dispatches one session MCP lifecycle action; the reducer updates optimistic state, AgentSideEffects invokes the provider, serverNameForCustomizationId checks the live inventory and then synchronously scans current session customizations. On a match, the provider lifecycle RPC is on the critical path. Start also schedules an inventory-list RPC in its finally block; that refresh is not awaited by the lifecycle promise. Stop awaits its lifecycle RPC.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One inbound action per user lifecycle request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same action reached AgentSideEffects and the provider before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This delivers the request to the provider; it exists before and after the diff.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Copilot SDK startServer or stopServer lifecycle RPC
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One lifecycle RPC per accepted action, serialized per server name. Start additionally triggers one asynchronous mcp.list inventory RPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: For a published-only ID missing from _live, the provider rejected the ID before issuing any lifecycle or inventory RPC. Existing live IDs already issued the same RPCs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The lifecycle RPC is awaited; the start-side inventory refresh is launched from finally but is not awaited.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Start or stop the effective MCP server selected by the SDK, potentially launching a local stdio server or connecting a configured remote server
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one server lifecycle operation per accepted action; same-name requests are serialized.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The published-only ID was rejected, so no server lifecycle operation occurred; live IDs already performed this work.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The requested server lifecycle dominates latency and is the intended effect of accepting the published ID.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The fallback cost grows with the number of current top-level customizations and their MCP children. It runs once per explicit lifecycle action; realistic effective cardinality is one target ID, not one provider call per customization. Existing live entries are checked first, and published-only entries become live after SDK reporting.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Copilot serializes lifecycle RPCs per server name with SequencerByKey; different server names may progress concurrently. The synchronous fallback scan itself is not parallelized and runs once before queueing.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The live inventory is the warm fast path. A published-only ID falls back to authoritative session state until the SDK reports it; unknown IDs also scan once and then stop. There is no separate fallback cache or negative cache, but the trigger is a low-frequency user action.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the fallback, call path, per-action cardinality, and per-server sequencer are explicit in the code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact customization count and provider RPC duration vary, but the new local work is one shallow state projection plus one linear flatten/find scan per explicit click. The heavier newly reachable provider operation is intentional functionality rather than redundant work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The PR adds one bounded linear lookup to a low-frequency control path and enables exactly the lifecycle operation the user requested; it does not fan out provider work across the collection.

Scenarios.Scenario: Codex MCP start/stop for a customization ID published before the thread inventory contains it
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A lifecycle action resolves the session, synchronously rebuilds controller state from the current per-thread inventory, refreshes the name-to-ID map, and then uses the new session-state fallback. For start, a successful fallback proceeds through lazy thread materialization, one configuration reload request, and a paginated status refresh. Stop currently performs no provider boundary after successful resolution.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One inbound action per explicit user request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical protocol dispatch occurred before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The action dispatch precedes provider handling and is unchanged by the diff.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Lazily materialize the Codex thread/connection when needed
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most once for an unmaterialized session, then reused by later operations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A published-only unresolved ID returned before materialization; accepted live IDs already followed this path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Materialization must finish before reload can proceed on a cold session.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one request per accepted start action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Published-only unresolved IDs did not issue reload; live IDs already issued one reload.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited on the start critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One or more requests according to nextCursor; grouping is by the full thread inventory, not per customization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Published-only unresolved IDs did not refresh; live IDs already performed the same full inventory refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All pages are awaited before start returns.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Resolution scales with current MCP inventory plus published top-level customizations and children. The fallback is one scan for one target ID. Status refresh scales by the provider's paginated server inventory, not by issuing one request per customization.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No lifecycle sequencer is present on the Codex start path; separate accepted actions can overlap. Normal UI dispatch is one action for the selected row, and this diff does not alter concurrency for already-live IDs. Stop performs only local resolution.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Current thread inventory populates the live path when available; published-only IDs use current session state. After reload/status refresh, inventory is refreshed and subsequent resolution can use live data. Unknown IDs do not cross provider boundaries.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the synchronous resolver, reload request, pagination loop, and absence of a stop boundary are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider inventory page count and cold materialization latency vary. The local added scan remains bounded by current published customizations, while the newly reachable expensive work is the intended start behavior.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The fallback only makes the requested lifecycle operation reachable for an exact current ID; it adds no per-item provider fan-out, and the local scan is not a hot path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Lifecycle resolution for an already-live ID or an unknown ID
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Already-live IDs return from the existing live-inventory loop before executing the added fallback. Unknown IDs execute the added session-state scan and then return without provider work.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Live resolution retains its prior behavior. A miss adds one O(C) flatten/find over current MCP customizations, where C is the effective total of top-level MCP entries and MCP children, once per explicit action.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No additional asynchronous work is created for unknown IDs. Provider-specific concurrency behavior is unchanged for live hits.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Live hits avoid the fallback on both cold and warm actions. Unknown misses are not negatively cached, but they require repeated explicit invalid actions to repeat the scan.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the early return and fallback placement are explicit in the changed method.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Only unusually large customization collections and repeated invalid lifecycle actions increase the added local CPU/allocation cost; neither is evidenced as a realistic hot path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. Existing successful requests incur no new work, and misses add only a bounded in-memory scan with no I/O, IPC, or subprocess operation.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over both changed files and all diff pages. Traced Copilot and Codex lifecycle callers, authoritative session-state access, fallback allocation/scanning, provider RPC/subprocess boundaries, cache behavior, and concurrency. The only added local cost is one fallback flatten/find on a low-frequency explicit control action; newly reachable lifecycle boundaries are the intended behavior, not redundant or scaling work. No valid performance finding and no qualifying performance-regression fix signal.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
